LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: NEATNESS AND LEGIBILITY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.1 Guided Writing (2 Sessions) • Vocabulary building • Sentences By the
Topic 3.2: Guided Writing: Neatness and Legibility

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Guided Writing: Neatness and Legibility
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why is it good to write clearly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify features of neat and legible handwriting
2. use basic descriptive words in writing neat and legible paragraphs
3. appreciate the skill of writing for effective communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Guided Writing: Neatness and Legibility

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Guided Writing: Neatness and Legibility

Teach
• Focus skill: identify features of neat and legible handwriting.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Guided Writing: Neatness and Legibility.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Guided Writing: Neatness and Legibility
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it good to write clearly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
